None of the legacy six are referenced by the frontend, any `.rpc/.functions.invoke` call, or any repo source; evidence-based supersession hypotheses are recorded per function in `governance/edge_deployment_plan.json` (e.g. `subscription-checkout` → `subscription-management`, cited from migration 20260821170000). 5. **RLS/security integrity track added as a convergent certification gate (2026-08-25):** Supabase Security Advisor reports 17 findings (predominantly `rls_disabled_in_public`). Retrieval tooling: `scripts/governance/retrieve_security_findings.py` (management API via `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, or the canonical SQL linter set via `SUPABASE_DB_URL`). Classification tooling: `scripts/governance/classify_security_findings.py` — every finding is bucketed `FIX_NOW | FIX_WITH_MIGRATION | GOVERNED_EXCEPTION | FALSE_STALE` using the repo's canonical data classification (tenant/business → `get_current_staff()`-scoped policy; webhook/service-ingestion → RLS-deny-to-clients + service-role ingestion; an exception requires a named compensating control). Constitutional constraints hard-wired: no `USING(true)`, no RLS disable to pass tests, `GOVERNED_EXCEPTION` requires a named compensating control, findings retrieve before any production change. `production_certification.py` now evaluates BOTH tracks — migration integrity AND RLS/security integrity — and the verdict is BLOCKED while the security track is unreviewed (`blocked`) or has unresolved `FIX_*` items. Enabling RLS alone is NOT resolution; policies must prove unauthorized access is denied while legitimate flows pass.
